questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with multiple hypopigmented anaesthetic patches and thickened ulnar and common peroneal nerves. Slit skin smear shows a bacillary index of 5+. Which WHO multidrug therapy regimen should be prescribed?
questions.exp: A bacillary index ≥2 at any site classifies a patient as multibacillary (MB) leprosy. WHO MB-MDT consists of Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily + Clofazimine 300 mg monthly and 50 mg daily, given for 12 months.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with flaccid bullae on the scalp, oral erosions, and a positive Nikolsky sign. Direct immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG and C3 deposition throughout the epidermis. Which target antigen is responsible?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris involves IgG autoantibodies against Desmoglein 3 (Dsg3), a desmosomal cadherin predominantly expressed in basal and suprabasal keratinocytes. Mucosal-dominant disease targets Dsg3 alone; mucocutaneous disease also targets Dsg1.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with malar rash, photosensitivity, and polyarthritis is being worked up for SLE. Which antibody is MOST specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibodies are highly specific (~95%) for SLE and correlate with disease activity and lupus nephritis. ANA is sensitive but not specific. Anti-histone is characteristic of drug-induced lupus; anti-Ro is associated with neonatal lupus and Sjogren syndrome.

questions.q: A 52-year-old fair-skinned man has a pigmented lesion on the back with irregular borders, four colours, and a diameter of 9 mm. Excisional biopsy confirms melanoma with Breslow thickness of 1.2 mm and no ulceration. What is the recommended surgical excision margin?
questions.exp: For melanoma with Breslow thickness 1.01-2 mm, NCCN/BAD guidelines recommend a 1 cm excision margin. Margins of 2 cm are used for thickness >2 mm. A 0.5 cm margin is used for melanoma in situ.

questions.q: An 8-year-old child presents with a scaly patch of alopecia on the scalp. Wood's lamp examination shows bright green fluorescence. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum species (M. canis, M. audouinii) produce bright green-yellow fluorescence under Wood's lamp due to pteridine metabolites within the hair shaft. Trichophyton species causing endothrix infection (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum) do NOT fluoresce.

questions.q: A 68-year-old diabetic develops grouped vesicles along the right V1 (ophthalmic) dermatome with a vesicle on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson's sign). Which complication is most immediately feared?
opts: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with ocular involvement
questions.exp: Hutchinson's sign — vesicles on the tip, side, or root of the nose — indicates involvement of the nasociliary branch of V1, which also supplies the globe. This predicts a high risk of herpes zoster ophthalmicus, potentially causing keratitis, uveitis, and blindness if untreated urgently.

questions.q: A 60-year-old presents with tense bullae on flexural areas without mucosal involvement. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. Which antigen is targeted?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is caused by IgG autoantibodies against BP180 (type XVII collagen, NC16A domain) and BP230. DIF shows linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ. Tense bullae and absent mucosal involvement distinguish BP from pemphigus vulgaris.

questions.q: A 38-year-old with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis has failed methotrexate and cyclosporine. The dermatologist prescribes a biologic that specifically targets IL-17A. Which drug is this?
questions.exp: Secukinumab and ixekizumab are monoclonal antibodies that directly neutralise IL-17A. Adalimumab targets TNF-alpha; ustekinumab targets the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23; guselkumab targets the p19 subunit of IL-23.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with intense nocturnal pruritus affecting the finger webs, wrists, and genitalia. Multiple family members are similarly affected. Which clinical finding is MOST diagnostic of scabies?
questions.exp: Burrows — linear or curved grey-white tracks caused by the tunnelling female mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis — are pathognomonic of scabies. Nocturnal pruritus and distribution are suggestive but not specific. Definitive diagnosis requires identifying mites, eggs, or scybala on dermoscopy or microscopy.

questions.q: A 30-year-old with intensely pruritic vesicles on the elbows, knees, and buttocks has granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillary tips on DIF. Which systemic condition is most commonly associated?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is the cutaneous manifestation of coeliac disease. Nearly all DH patients have silent gluten-sensitive enteropathy; a strict gluten-free diet is therapeutic for both. Granular IgA at dermal papillae is the DIF hallmark.

questions.q: A 24-year-old sexually active male presents with a single painless ulcer on the coronal sulcus with firm, non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochaetes. What is the first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) is treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose — the WHO and CDC first-line recommendation. Doxycycline for 14 days is the alternative in penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 26-year-old presents with a painless unilateral inguinal mass with a characteristic groove sign (nodes above and below the inguinal ligament). Pus aspirated from the bubo shows intracytoplasmic inclusions. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, and L3. The groove sign is characteristic. Treatment is doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman develops heliotrope rash around the eyes, periorbital oedema, and violaceous flat-topped papules over the dorsal knuckles. Which skin sign is considered PATHOGNOMONIC of dermatomyositis?
questions.exp: Gottron's papules — violaceous, flat-topped papules over the MCP and IP joints — are pathognomonic of dermatomyositis. Heliotrope rash, V-sign, and shawl sign are characteristic but not pathognomonic, as they can appear in other conditions.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy with severe nodulocystic acne is being considered for systemic therapy. Which agent requires enrolment in a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) programme due to its teratogenic potential?
questions.exp: Isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid) is a potent teratogen causing craniofacial, cardiac, thymic, and CNS defects. The iPLEDGE programme (USA) and similar REMS schemes mandate monthly pregnancy tests, dual contraception, and prescriber/patient registration before and during therapy.

questions.q: A 70-year-old has a pearly lesion on the nose with poorly defined, waxy, indurated borders. Biopsy shows strands of tumour cells embedded in a fibrous stroma with minimal peripheral palisading. Which BCC subtype carries the HIGHEST risk of recurrence after standard excision?
questions.exp: Morphoeic (sclerosing) BCC infiltrates along tissue planes with poorly defined clinical margins, making standard excision inadequate. It has the highest recurrence rate (~33% vs ~5% for nodular). Mohs micrographic surgery is the preferred treatment for this subtype.

questions.q: A known lepromatous leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden-onset painful erythematous nodules over the thighs and legs, fever, uveitis, and testicular tenderness. What is this reaction and the immediate treatment?
opts: Type 2 reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum) — treat with thalidomide or prednisolone
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (Type 2 reaction) occurs in BL/LL patients and is an immune-complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity) reaction. It presents with painful skin nodules, fever, and systemic involvement (iritis, orchitis, neuritis). Thalidomide or prednisolone is used; MDT is continued throughout.

questions.q: A 32-year-old with a mechanobullous disorder has linear IgG at the dermoepidermal junction on DIF. Salt-split skin testing shows IgG deposits on the dermal side (floor) of the split. Which antigen is targeted?
questions.exp: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) targets type VII collagen (anchoring fibrils at the BMZ). On 1M NaCl salt-split skin, BP and MMP antibodies bind the roof (epidermal side), while EBA antibodies bind the floor (dermal side) — a key distinguishing test.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4 count of 120 cells/uL presents with asymptomatic violaceous plaques on the lower legs and hard palate. Biopsy shows spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces. Which herpesvirus is causally linked?
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is caused by Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8, KSHV). It is an AIDS-defining illness. Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and haemosiderin deposits. HAART-induced immune restoration is integral to treatment alongside chemotherapy for advanced disease.

questions.q: A 25-year-old with generalised vitiligo achieves complete stability with no new lesions for 2 years. Which treatment modality offers the best chance of lasting repigmentation in STABLE vitiligo?
questions.exp: Surgical procedures — suction blister grafting, split-thickness grafting, or MKTP — are preferred for stable vitiligo (no progression for ≥1-2 years). MKTP allows large surface coverage from a small donor site with excellent cosmetic results. Phototherapy and topical immunomodulators are used for active disease.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman has recurring widespread wheals with angioedema for 3 months. Allergy testing is negative and no trigger is identified. What is the first-line pharmacological treatment for chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU)?
opts: Second-generation non-sedating H1 antihistamine (e.g., cetirizine 10 mg daily)
questions.exp: EAACI/GA2LEN guidelines recommend non-sedating H1 antihistamines as first-line therapy for CSU, with dose up-titration up to fourfold if inadequate. Omalizumab is third-line (after antihistamines and cyclosporine or other immunosuppressants).

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with asymptomatic hypopigmented, fine-scaling macules on the chest and back that worsen in summer. KOH preparation shows short hyphae and clusters of round spores in a 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Pityriasis (tinea) versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (M. globosa), a lipophilic commensal yeast. The 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern (short curved hyphae + spherical spores) on KOH is pathognomonic. Treatment: topical azoles, selenium sulphide, or oral fluconazole/itraconazole.

questions.q: A 32-year-old epileptic patient started on carbamazepine 6 weeks ago develops fever, facial oedema, generalised morbilliform eruption, cervical lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia (1800 cells/uL), and elevated transaminases. What is the diagnosis?
opts: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
questions.exp: DRESS typically appears 2-8 weeks after drug initiation due to HHV-6 reactivation (long latency distinguishes it from SJS/TEN). Diagnostic criteria (RegiSCAR): fever, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytosis or eosinophilia, and ≥2 organ involvements. Aromatic anticonvulsants are common culprits.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with a painful genital ulcer with soft, undermined edges, purulent base, and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Gram stain shows gram-negative coccobacilli in a 'school of fish' pattern. What is the recommended treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) presents with painful soft ulcers and suppurative bubo. CDC-recommended regimens include azithromycin 1 g orally single dose, ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose, or ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD for 3 days. The school of fish pattern is characteristic on Gram stain.

questions.q: During nail examination in a psoriasis patient, which nail change is considered MOST specific for psoriasis compared to other dermatological conditions?
questions.exp: The oil drop sign (salmon patch) — a yellowish-brown discolouration visible through the nail plate representing subungual psoriasis — is highly specific for psoriasis. Pitting is common but also seen in alopecia areata; onycholysis and Beau's lines are non-specific.

questions.q: In the immunopathogenesis of atopic dermatitis, which cytokine axis primarily drives allergic inflammation and epidermal barrier dysfunction?
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis is predominantly Th2-driven. IL-4 and IL-13 promote IgE class switching, suppress filaggrin expression (impairing the epidermal barrier), and perpetuate chronicity. Dupilumab blocks the shared IL-4Ralpha receptor subunit, effectively inhibiting both IL-4 and IL-13 signalling.

questions.q: A 44-year-old woman with a history of urticaria pigmentosa develops flushing, diarrhoea, and hypotension after NSAIDs. Bone marrow biopsy shows dense mast cell aggregates with CD117+ spindle-shaped mast cells. Which serum marker confirms systemic mastocytosis?
questions.exp: A baseline serum tryptase level persistently >20 ng/mL is a WHO 2022 minor diagnostic criterion for systemic mastocytosis, reflecting total mast cell burden. The major criterion is multifocal dense mast cell infiltrates (>15 cells/aggregate) in bone marrow. KIT D816V mutation is also a minor criterion.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine for rheumatoid arthritis develops asymptomatic pigmentary changes on sun-exposed areas and the hard palate. What is the characteristic pigmentation associated with antimalarial drugs?
questions.exp: Antimalarial drugs (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine) cause blue-grey (slate-grey) pigmentation, especially on the face, shins, and hard palate. It results from accumulation of drug-melanin complexes and haemosiderin in macrophages. Minocycline and amiodarone cause similar blue-grey discolouration via different mechanisms.

questions.q: In wound healing, which growth factor is the PRINCIPAL mediator of angiogenesis during the proliferative phase?
questions.exp: VEGF (particularly VEGF-A) is the master regulator of angiogenesis in wound healing, promoting endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and new vessel formation. PDGF drives fibroblast and smooth muscle cell recruitment; EGF promotes re-epithelialisation; TGF-beta regulates collagen synthesis and remodelling.

questions.q: A dermatologist selects a biologic that specifically targets the p19 subunit of IL-23 for a patient with severe plaque psoriasis who failed anti-TNF therapy. Which drug has this mechanism?
questions.exp: Guselkumab (Tremfya) and risankizumab selectively block IL-23 by targeting its unique p19 subunit, sparing IL-12. Ustekinumab targets the shared p40 subunit of both IL-12 and IL-23. Secukinumab and ixekizumab block IL-17A; brodalumab blocks the IL-17RA receptor.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman on sulphonamides develops epidermal detachment involving 35% of body surface area with positive Nikolsky sign, mucositis, and conjunctivitis. Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal necrosis. What is the correct classification?
opts: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) — defined as <10% BSA involvement
SJS/TEN overlap — defined as 10-30% BSA involvement
Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) — defined as >30% BSA involvement
questions.exp: TEN (Lyell syndrome) is defined by epidermal detachment of >30% BSA with full-thickness epidermal necrosis on histology. SJS affects <10% BSA and SJS/TEN overlap 10-30%. SSSS occurs mainly in children and shows superficial (subcorneal) cleavage without mucosal involvement. Sulphonamides, allopurinol, and anticonvulsants are common culprits.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis develops accelerated hypertension and a rapidly rising creatinine. Which autoantibody is characteristically associated with scleroderma renal crisis?
questions.exp: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies are strongly associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and are a major risk factor for scleroderma renal crisis (SRC), presenting with accelerated hypertension and microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia. Anti-Scl-70 is linked with ILD and dcSSc; anti-centromere with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome).
